title: Orb internet pub/sub — open decisions
notes: ADR-0001 complete. Q39 updated: app account 019051664753 (orbnet-dev); DNS stays 514723210267 (russell-personal).

Q0a.decision: Canonical domain orbnet.app (apex portal, www→apex, api.orbnet.app, gw.orbnet.app). Placeholder wireframe-orb logo (marble/adr/orb-logo.svg). Mailboxes to provision: noreply@ (magic links), hello@, support@, abuse@, security@, billing@ (later). MX: SES or Cloudflare Email Routing until Workspace. Stub apple-app-site-association and assetlinks.json on apex.

Q0b.decision: Fan-out ≤2KB envelope everywhere; body stored once, GET on open, hard cap 1MB UTF-8. No 128KB vs 1MB fetch tiers. Bots default envelopes-only. Meter envelope count + body-fetch GB.

Q1.decision: First users: operator, Marble, and one friend/family. Spike includes polished public signup (magic-link create account → first topic → copy publish key), not API-only. Friend must finish without SSH. Marble uses the API; humans use the portal.

Q2.decision: Hosted SaaS only in v1 (orbnet.app). Self-host binary is phase 3.

Q3.decision: Do not compete as a ntfy clone. Optional BYO ntfy topic as a 2KB wakeup sink. Optional ntfy-compatible POST gateway on api.orbnet.app later.

Q4.decision: Public topics are listen-only. Only keyed publishers may POST. Topic URL is not a password.

Q5.decision: Starting unpaid is fine but we have to architect for paid so enabling it later is easy, leave stubs

Q6.decision: Ops-terminal tone: dense markdown inbox, not chat bubbles, not consumer-calm marketing.

Q7.decision: Image support in markdown on v1, we want rich readable agent reports with SVG style diagrams as first class

Q8.decision: Markdown as default, publisher can flag as json if they want pure json to keep client parsing trouble free

Q9.decision: The message priority should be set by the receiver based on client settings for the subscription/channel and the receiver's mood, not the sender

Q10.decision: Free: 7d body retention private, 24h public. Envelope index 7d both. Tune with plan later.

Q11.decision: Same topic. Humans and bots both get envelopes. Bots opt into body fetch / durable offsets. No separate topic type.

Q12.decision: v1 flat feed grouped only by topic. Optional client-side group by run_id if present. No threads-as-product.

Q13.decision: Track read receipts, senders should be able to see status of how many clients received a message to track stats, especially for monetization later

Q14.decision: If not specified the server breaks up into envelope/body; if sender specifies they can control envelope and body explicitly.

Q15.decision: Email magic link required to create topics. GitHub/Google OIDC optional in addition, not instead, until passkeys.

Q16.decision: v1 keys are topic-scoped. Account-level admin key (orb_ak_) manages topics/keys but does not publish unless explicitly granted.

Q17.decision: Anonymous OK for public subscribe. Optional subscriber key only for private/paid or for bots that want higher rate limits / durable cursor.

Q18.decision: Invite is single-topic. Org bundles are v1.5.

Q19.decision: Invite: max uses default 10, expiry 7d, cap 5 devices per grant. Owner can revoke.

Q20.decision: Anonymous device key signs a merge to the new account; subscriptions unioned. Conflicts: account prefs win.

Q21.decision: Web+desktop only for now, don't fuss with ntfy bridge

Q22.decision: Linux: StatusNotifierItem / AppIndicator. GNOME: notifications still work if tray is hidden; document that.

Q23.decision: macOS: menu bar extra + optional dock. Default: menu bar, no dock bounce unless priority ≥4.

Q24.decision: MVP: unsigned/raw binaries + Homebrew-style script. Notarize when we have the Apple account.

Q25.decision: Operator’s personal Apple/Google accounts until a company exists. Don’t block desktop on store listings.

Q26.decision: No UnifiedPush in v1. FCM when we have an Android app. Until then ntfy distributor is the user’s problem.

Q27.decision: Yes — web portal is system of record for billing even if the user only uses CLI.

Q28.decision: No cross-device suppression in v1. Each device honors its own prefs. Presence is a later project.

Q29.decision: Subscriber always wins: global DND > per-topic mute > receiver-configured loudness (not sender priority).

Q30.decision: No un-muteable urgent. Subscriber always sovereign, including security-ish pings.

Q31.decision: Digest = time bucket (hourly/daily) of envelopes, not a new body. Off by default.

Q32.decision: No Orb-hosted ntfy. v1 does not fuss with an ntfy bridge (see Q21). BYO ntfy remains a later optional sink.

Q33.decision: Lock-screen postcard = title only (or title + 80 chars if user enables preview). Default title-only for private topics.

Q34.decision: Spike/unpaid v1: DynamoDB on-demand + Lambda + API Gateway WebSocket (ADR-0003 A). No Postgres LISTEN, no Redis, no JetStream until fan-out or SQL hurts. Later: self-run NATS JetStream on ECS. Not Synadia Cloud on day one.

Q36.decision: No per-tenant JetStream accounts in v1. One stream with subject per topic id. Isolate later if noisy.

Q37.decision: Soft cap 10k subscribers/topic in v1. Envelope fanout is cheap; don’t promise millions.

Q39.decision: Terraform against AWS account 019051664753 (CLI profile orbnet-dev, IAM user admin) for spike/MVP compute, SES, ACM. DNS/Route53 hosted zone orbnet.app (Z057369368K37F0A6J46) remains in personal account 514723210267 (CLI profile russell-personal, IAM user rendicott). Cross-account aliases and ACM/SES validation CNAMEs; do not create a second hosted zone in the app account. LLC/prod is a future new account + Terraform re-apply, not a rename of 514723210267.

Q40.decision: CloudWatch + optional Grafana Cloud. OpenTelemetry traces on publish/fetch.

Q41.decision: No charges until a legal entity exists. Free caps only. Stripe later under that entity.

Q42.decision: Free: 3 public + 1 private topic, 10k envelopes/month, 2GB body-fetch, 1GB stored bodies.

Q43.decision: Defer price points until we have usage. No public pricing page in spike.

Q44.decision: No EU region in v1. Disclose US processing in privacy policy.

Q45.decision: No encryption in v1 but stub and prepare. Mini ADR explores encryption challenges.

Q46.decision: Markdown images in v1. ToS + report + freeze now; automated CSAM detection later.

Q47.decision: Small MCP server (publish, list envelopes, fetch body) once HTTP API exists. Not a spike blocker.

Q48.decision: v1 one-way. Human reply / agent.ask callbacks are v2 with auth on callback.

Q49.decision: Encourage orb.agent.v1 front matter. No enforced schema registry in v1.

Q50.decision: X-Orb-Path hop list on publish. Server appends current topic id; 409 if a topic repeats or hop count > 8. SDKs copy the header on republish. Bare curl with no header is hop 1.

Q51.decision: Marble has no email/Telegram today. Orb is the first human notification sink, not a replacement of existing channels.

Q52.decision: Optional ntfy-compatible POST https://api.orbnet.app/ntfy/{topic} after native API. Not spike-critical.

Q53.decision: Operator is on-call. No pager rotation. Best-effort SLA.

Q54.decision: First 90 days under a few hundred USD. No Apple/Google fees until store apps.

Q55.decision: Server+clients closed until there’s a product. Protocol/docs can be public later.

Q56.decision: Success: Marble publishes to a private orbnet.app topic; Mac tray shows envelope; opening fetches markdown body; one publish key. Phone optional via BYO ntfy later (not a v1 bridge).
